item.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts missiles as debris falls near energy sites
item.description: Saudi Arabia's defense ministry announced early Tuesday that air defenses intercepted multiple ballistic missiles fired toward the kingdom's Eastern Province, with debris falling near energy facilities. The ministry said damage assessment was underway but did not identify the source of the attack.

item.title: UN Security Council to vote on Strait of Hormuz resolution
item.description: The United Nations Security Council is scheduled to vote on Tuesday at 11 a.m. Eastern Time on a watered-down resolution addressing Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, diplomatic sources told AFP, capping weeks of fractious negotiations that saw the original text stripped of its most forceful provisions. The vote comes just nine hours before President Donald Trump's self-imposed deadline for Iran to agree to a deal or face strikes on its power plants and bridges.

item.title: Iran launches fresh missile barrage at southern Israel
item.description: Iran fired a new wave of ballistic missiles at southern Israel on Monday, targeting areas including Beersheba, Dimona, and the wider Negev region after a hours-long lull in attacks, as the broader war between Iran and Israel entered its sixth week. The strikes came alongside a coordinated Houthi assault on the Red Sea city of Eilat, marking a new phase of multi-front escalation.

item.title: Israel orders evacuation of 41 towns in southern Lebanon
item.description:
The Israeli military issued urgent evacuation orders on Monday evening directing residents of 41 towns and residential clusters in southern Lebanon to move north of the Zahrani River, according to the Qatar News Agency and local Lebanese media. The directive, delivered by the Israeli military's Arabic-language spokesman Colonel Avichay Adraee, came amid a day of intensified airstrikes across southern Lebanon, Beirut's southern suburbs, and areas previously considered safe from bombardment.

The orders mark the latest expansion of what Israel has described as a security buffer zone, which has grown from the Litani River northward to the Zahrani River — roughly 40 kilometers from the Israeli border — encompassing nearly 15 percent of Lebanon's total land area.

item.title: Iran-launched drone kills couple in Erbil village
item.description:
An explosive-laden drone launched from Iran struck a civilian home in the village of Zargazawi in Erbil province early Tuesday, killing a married couple and marking the latest deadly escalation in a weeks-long aerial campaign against Iraq's Kurdistan Region.

The Kurdistan Region's Directorate General of Counter-Terrorism (CTD) confirmed that the drone hit the home at approximately 12:15 a.m. local time on Tuesday in the Dara Shakran sub-district, killing Musa Anwar Rasul and Mujda Asaad Hasan. The CTD condemned the attack as a violation of international law and a war crime. Air defense systems intercepted multiple other drones over Erbil the same night, including at least four targeting the US consulate, according to Shafaq News.

item.title: Iranian drone strike wounds 15 US troops at Kuwait air base
item.description: An Iranian drone strike on Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait overnight on Sunday wounded 15 American service members, with most having already returned to duty, according to CBS News, citing two US officials with knowledge of the attack. The strike marks the latest in a series of Iranian assaults on US positions in the Gulf since the war began on February 28.

item.title: Iran's UN envoy accuses Trump of inciting terrorism
item.description: Iran's ambassador to the United Nations accused President Donald Trump of inciting terrorism in a letter sent to UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, as the war between the United States and Iran entered its sixth week with a critical deadline looming.

item.title: Iran strike on Saudi Arabia’s Jubail industrial hub sparks fire
item.description:
Iranian ballistic missiles and drones struck Saudi Arabia's Jubail Industrial City in the Eastern Province on Monday, sparking fires at petrochemical facilities in the world's largest industrial complex and deepening fears of a catastrophic disruption to global chemical supply chains.

Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Defence confirmed its air defense systems intercepted seven ballistic missiles aimed at the Eastern Province, according to Reuters, though debris fell near energy facilities. Social media footage showed large fires engulfing sections of the industrial zone, with the full extent of damage still unclear as emergency crews responded.

item.title: Artemis II crew witnesses solar eclipse after shattering distance record
item.description: The four astronauts aboard NASA's Artemis II mission witnessed a total solar eclipse on Monday evening as their Orion spacecraft swung around the far side of the Moon, capping a day of record-breaking achievements during humanity's first crewed lunar voyage in more than half a century.

item.title: SpaceX details record IPO plans, eyes June roadshow
item.description: SpaceX outlined specifics of what is expected to be the largest initial public offering in history at a meeting with its banking syndicate on Monday night, detailing plans for a roadshow beginning the week of June 8 and an unprecedented push to include retail investors, according to Reuters, citing two people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Iran urges youth to form human chains around power plants as Trump deadline looms
item.description: As President Donald Trump's 8 p.m. Eastern Time deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approaches on Tuesday, Iran's Ministry of Sports and Youth has called on young Iranians to form symbolic human chains around the country's key power plants beginning at 2 p.m. local time — roughly 13 hours before the ultimatum expires.

item.title: Iran war energy crisis fuels surge in Chinese clean tech exports
item.description:
The war in Iran has upended global fossil fuel markets, and China — the world's dominant producer of solar panels, batteries, and electric vehicles — is emerging as a prime beneficiary of the resulting scramble for clean energy alternatives.

Even before the conflict began on February 28, China's clean energy technology exports were surging. Data highlighted by Lauri Myllyvirta of the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air shows that the value of those exports rose 44% in January and February 2026, reaching $41 billion, led by EVs and batteries. The disruption to fossil fuel supply chains has only accelerated interest from foreign buyers.

item.title: Trump's Tuesday deadline for Iran looms as oil markets surge
item.description: Oil markets swung wildly on Monday as President Donald Trump issued his most forceful ultimatum yet to Iran, demanding the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz by Tuesday evening or face devastating strikes on the country's infrastructure. U.S. crude briefly exceeded $114 per barrel before retreating, while premiums for physical barrels of American oil climbed to record levels as buyers across Asia and Europe scrambled for supply.

item.title: Air India, WestJet raise fuel surcharges as Iran war doubles jet fuel costs
item.description: Two major carriers on opposite sides of the globe announced fuel surcharge increases this week as the ongoing U.S.-Israeli military campaign in Iran continues to roil global energy markets. WestJet will introduce a temporary $60 surcharge on companion voucher bookings starting April 8, while Air India is overhauling its surcharge structure for both domestic and international flights effective April 8 and April 10, respectively.

item.title: King Fahd Causeway reopens after Iranian missile strikes on Saudi Arabia
item.description:
The King Fahd Causeway, the sole road link between Saudi Arabia and the island kingdom of Bahrain, reopened on Tuesday after a brief closure prompted by Iranian ballistic missile strikes targeting Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province. The King Fahd Causeway Authority announced on X that traffic on the bridge was "back to normal after a temporary suspension" that had been imposed as a precautionary measure.

The reopening came hours after authorities halted all vehicle movement across the 25-kilometer bridge in the early hours of Tuesday, as Iran launched seven ballistic missiles toward Saudi Arabia's eastern region. Saudi Arabia's defense ministry said it intercepted and destroyed the missiles, though debris fell near energy facilities. A major fire erupted at the Al Jubail Industrial City, the Middle East's largest industrial hub and a center of petrochemical and oil refining operations, after what open-source intelligence accounts described as a ballistic missile and drone attack.

item.title: Oil rises, futures slip as Trump's Iran deadline looms
item.description: Global markets entered a period of heightened tension on Tuesday as President Donald Trump's deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz — set for 8 p.m. Eastern Time — loomed over trading floors worldwide. Oil prices climbed while U.S. equity futures slipped, and cryptocurrency markets wavered as investors weighed the prospect of a last-minute diplomatic breakthrough against the threat of a devastating military escalation.

item.title: Saudi Arabia closes Bahrain causeway after Iranian missile strikes
item.description: Saudi Arabia shut down the King Fahd Causeway, the sole road link connecting it to Bahrain, early on Tuesday as Iranian ballistic missiles targeted the kingdom's oil-rich Eastern Province, according to the Associated Press. The closure came hours before a deadline set by President Donald Trump for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or face strikes on its power plants and bridges.

item.title: Iran war energy shock accelerates global return to nuclear power
item.description: The war between Israel and Iran has upended global energy markets, cutting off roughly one-fifth of the world's liquefied natural gas supply and prompting a rapid reassessment of nuclear energy across Asia and beyond. Countries that had retreated from atomic power after the 2011 Fukushima disaster are now racing to restart reactors, extend plant lifespans, and build new capacity as LNG prices surge and supply reliability crumbles.

item.title: Dangote refinery ramps up African exports amid Iran war
item.description:
Nigeria's Dangote refinery, the largest in Africa, has stepped up exports of gasoline and urea fertilizer to countries across the continent as supply disruptions caused by the war on Iran continue to squeeze global energy and commodity markets, owner Aliko Dangote said on Monday.

The refinery, operating at its full capacity of 650,000 barrels per day, has shipped approximately 17 cargoes of gasoline to other African nations, with urea fertilizer exports also climbing as buyers scramble for alternatives to traditional Middle East and Gulf suppliers, according to Reuters. Dangote said the facility had helped cushion the crisis both in Nigeria and across the continent.

item.title: IEA chief says Middle East war will accelerate renewables shift
item.description:
The worst energy crisis in modern history will ultimately speed the world's pivot to renewable energy, nuclear power, and electric vehicles, International Energy Agency chief Fatih Birol predicted in an interview published Tuesday with the French newspaper Le Figaro.

Birol described the current energy shock, triggered by the Middle East war and Iran's de facto blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, as "more serious than those of 1973, 1979 and 2022 combined". Yet the IEA executive director said there were "reasons to be optimistic" about how the upheaval would reshape the global energy system.
